title: Harden generated-output contract and resolve MaterialRegion submesh semantics
description:
## Summary

Strengthen the generated-output contract so it cannot represent states the generator never intentionally builds, and resolve the under-specified `MaterialRegion` submesh semantics. An external audit (P2/P1-P2) found `GeneratedCreature`, `GeometryItem`, and `MaterialRegion` expose mutable fields/list and encode the implicit-surface item by positional `Geometry[0]`, while mesh-asset output preserves multiple submeshes that `MaterialRegion` cannot express.

Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-deep-dive-code-review-2026-09-05.md` P1/P2 (MaterialRegion submesh), P2 (GeneratedCreature weak DTO), P2 (item-0 positional primitive obsession), P2 (O(n) `TryFindGeometryForPart`). Verified at current HEAD `99fe6ad`. Broad owner family: TSK-0095 (generated-output contract / stage boundaries). No existing TSK owns the output-model hardening.

## Scope

`Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/GeneratedCreature.cs` and its construction site (`CreatureMeshGenerator.Assemble`):

- Make `GeneratedCreature` expose `IReadOnlyList<GeometryItem>` with one internal construction path; make `GeometryItem`/`MaterialRegion`/`RigBindingMetadata` read-only after construction via constructor initialization, keeping `Assemble` as the only factory.
- Add semantic accessors (e.g. `TryGetImplicitSurface(out GeometryItem)`); keep `MainMesh`/positional ordering only as compatibility until callers migrate.
- Resolve the `MaterialRegion` multi-submesh ambiguity by choosing one explicit model: (1) `MaterialRegion` owns `SubmeshIndex + StartIndex + IndexCount + MaterialKey`; (2) material assignment is by submesh and `MaterialRegion` is removed for mesh assets; or (3) the generator flattens submeshes into one index stream as an explicit invariant. Record the choice in an ADR or the type docs.
- Optionally back `TryFindGeometryForPart` with an ordinal dictionary while preserving deterministic list order, only if a real consumer shows repeated lookups.
- Do not change generated geometry behavior or introduce a rendering framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A malformed `GeometryItem` state cannot be constructed through the public factory.
- `TryGetImplicitSurface` returns the semantic implicit-surface item; callers no longer depend on positional `Geometry[0]` for new code.
- Multi-submesh mesh-asset output has deterministic, documented material-region semantics under the chosen model.
- Mirrored items retain stable source identity while generated collection identity remains distinguishable.
- Existing generation and preview tests remain green.

## Validation

Focused runtime/EditMode tests for the construction boundary and the multi-submesh material-region semantics. Run the full Unity suites. Static source inspection alone cannot close this task.

## Findings

- `GeneratedCreature.Geometry` is a mutable `List<GeometryItem>`; `GeometryItem` exposes mutable source/type/mesh/regions/binding fields; `MaterialRegions`/`RigBinding` are mutable after construction.
- `MainMesh` assumes `Geometry[0]` is the implicit surface — positional primitive obsession even though `GeometryType`/`ImplicitSurfaceSourceId` already suggest semantic lookup.
- `BuildMeshAssetItem` preserves each submesh independently but builds one `MaterialRegion` with `IndexCount = mesh.triangles.Length`; no submesh identity exists, leaving the intended per-submesh range semantics ambiguous.
- `TryFindGeometryForPart` is an O(n) scan in a model otherwise moving to keyed access.

## Blockers

None known. Existing `ResolvedCreatureSnapshot`, `BoneSnapshot`, and `PosedSkeleton` already model immutable result objects, so this strengthens rather than introduces a pattern.

## Next Step

Introduce the construction boundary and semantic accessors, then decide and document the `MaterialRegion` submesh model with tests.

comments.body:
## Implementation evidence (sprint round 2)

Hardened the generated-output contract and resolved MaterialRegion submesh semantics (ADR-009).

### Contract hardening
- `GeneratedCreature.Geometry` is now `IReadOnlyList<GeometryItem>` over a private list; single internal construction path `AddGeometry(GeometryItem)` (rejects null); `CreatureMeshGenerator.Assemble` is the only factory. Consumers cannot mutate after generation.
- `GeometryItem`/`MaterialRegion`/`RigBindingMetadata` are immutable (read-only props set by internal constructors that reject malformed states: null mesh/part id, negative start/count/submesh, null material key).
- Added semantic `TryGetImplicitSurface(out GeometryItem)`; `MainMesh` kept as compatibility now backed by the accessor. New code/tests use the semantic accessor, not positional `Geometry[0]`.
- `TryFindGeometryForPart` intentionally left O(n) (no consumer shows repeated lookups); documented.

### MaterialRegion model (chosen + recorded)
Chose option 1 (submesh-index range model): `MaterialRegion = SubmeshIndex + StartIndex + IndexCount + MaterialKey`. A keyed mesh-asset part emits one region per submesh (each the submesh's full index range, `IndexCount = mesh.GetTriangles(s).Length`), fixing the old submesh-0-only `mesh.triangles.Length` ambiguity. Single-submesh part yields one region (matches prior behavior + explicit SubmeshIndex). Recorded explicitly in `docs/adr/ADR-009-generatedoutput-immutability-and-materialregion-submesh-model.md` with rationale against options 2/3.

### Assembly seam (flagged)
`Runtime/AssemblyInfo.cs` now also grants `InternalsVisibleTo("ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor")` so the editor preview-ownership test can fabricate the now-immutable GeneratedCreature through the internal path (it could no longer use the removed public mutable `Geometry.Add`). One-way grant; no runtime->editor reference; mirrors the sibling grant. Deliberate, reviewed.

Files changed:
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/GeneratedCreature.cs`
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/CreatureMeshGenerator.cs`
- `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/AssemblyInfo.cs`
- `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Editor/CreaturePreviewControllerOwnershipTests.cs` (migrated off public mutation)
- `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/GeneratedCreatureTests.cs` (new contract tests)
- `docs/adr/ADR-009-...md` (new ADR)

## Validation evidence
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- dotnet builds (`Runtime`, `Editor`, `Tests.Runtime`, `Tests.Editor`, all `--no-restore`): pass 0W/0E.
- Unity EditMode (report-backed): `CreatureGenerationConfigTests` + `CreaturePreviewControllerOwnershipTests` 9/9.
- Unity PlayMode **independently re-run by orchestrator**: `GeneratedCreatureTests` 20/20 passed, incl. new `Generate_MultiSubmeshMeshPart_EmitsOneRegionPerSubmesh`, `GeneratedCreature_TryGetImplicitSurface_ReturnsSemanticImplicitItem`, `GeneratedCreature_AddGeometry_NullItem_ThrowsDomainException`, `GeometryItem_CannotBeConstructedWithNullMesh`, `GeneratedCreature_ExposesReadOnlyGeometryCollection`. (The MCP EditMode runner does not discover Runtime-assembly fixtures, so the focused gate was run in PlayMode.)

## Residual risk
New runtime contract tests were not executed in EditMode (fixture lives in the Runtime assembly), but were independently executed in PlayMode 20/20. Generated geometry behavior is unchanged (single-submesh material output identical plus explicit SubmeshIndex). Full-suite confirmation is covered by the broader runtime/EditMode suites on the next full pass.
